item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Seconding Agent MacLeod above.

Really wanted to upvote because the idea is awesome, but the execution is basically everything bad about Series I articles lumped into one. Breach of clinical tone is rampant, the few tests that are present go straight for animal-human brain swaps and cross-species sex reassignment, there are needless redactions that look like they're included just to redact things, it is super lolFoundation, and basic wiki syntax/paragraph reworking could be used to clean up the flow and presentation greatly.

The description needs a serious trim, because the entire article practically lost me before we even got to the anomalous part. You could basically cut the description in half, replace all of the minutiae in the first half with one sentence explaining what the exterior looks like, and start it with "When connected to a suitable power source…"

In short, this SCP has not aged well at all and is in need of a faithful rewrite to modernize it. Here's to hoping that a good chunk of older site members revisit this and reconsider their +1 so that it can get a much needed update.

item.title: Is the Reassembled Organism the Original, or is it Just a Clone?
item.content:encoded:
What would happen to the soul of the disassembled organism? It's like when you consider a teleporter and you wonder if the person who appears at the other side is really the same person who entered the teleporter or a clone!

Would the reassembled organism be the original, or would it be a clone? In other words, if you used this, would "you" come out after reassembly, or would it be a clone and "you" would be dead?

An article on this kind of subject can be found here, specifically at the "The Teletransporter Thought Experiment" and the "The Body Scattering Test" sections.

After rereading this, an idea popped into my head:
An earlier Foundation or alternate Foundation-like group was trying to contain an Able-like entity. They had killed him temporarily, and, as a last resort, stuck him in this to disassemble him. It worked, until one of the blocks started shaking and shaking uncontrollably, before finally bursting free.
The result, of course, was SCP-058. The location of the other component blocks is currently unknown.

Anyways, that's my new favorite not-canon-at-all origin story. I like this SCP.
